description:
Fetch and parse the complete equity holdings table from a specific SEC 13F-HR
        filing. Any institution managing more than $100M in US equities must file
        quarterly — this reveals their exact portfolio positions.

        Returns one record per position:
          - name_of_issuer        — company name (e.g. 'APPLE INC')
          - cusip                 — 9-character CUSIP identifier
          - title_of_class        — share class (e.g. 'COM', 'ADR')
          - value_thousands       — market value in thousands USD
          - value_usd             — market value in USD
          - shares_or_principal   — number of shares (SH) or principal amount (PRN)
          - investment_discretion — SOLE, SHARED, or OTHER
          - put_call              — 'Put' or 'Call' for options; null for equities
          - voting_sole/shared/none — voting authority breakdown

        PRIMARY USE: Step 2 of institutional holdings workflow. Obtain cik and
        accession_no from SearchEdgar13F or GetEdgarCompanyFilings, then call this
        tool to get the actual positions.

        Use min_value_thousands to filter noise (e.g. 1000 = positions ≥ $1M).
        Use sort_by='value_desc' to see the largest positions first.
        Use limit (default 100) and offset for pagination — large filers can
        have 3,000+ positions. Check _has_more in the response to know if more
        pages exist.

        Source: SEC EDGAR Archives (13F infotable XML). No API key required.

Holdings13FParams.description:
Parameters for fetching the full parsed holdings table from a specific SEC
13F-HR filing. Returns every equity position (name, CUSIP, market value,
shares) reported by the institutional filer for that quarter.
Use SearchEdgar13F to discover accession numbers, then feed them here.

accession_no.description: Accession number of the 13F-HR filing to parse. Format: 'XXXXXXXXXX-YY-NNNNNN' (with dashes). Obtain from SearchEdgar13F or GetEdgarCompanyFilings. Example: '0001350694-24-000012'.
accession_no.title: Accession No

additional_display_fields.description: List of additional fields to display (e.g. ['firm_name', 'rep_name'])
additional_display_fields.title: Additional Display Fields

cik.description: SEC CIK of the institutional filer (e.g. a hedge fund or asset manager). Obtain from SearchEdgar13F or GetEdgarCompanyFilings. Example: '1350694' (Bridgewater Associates).
cik.title: Cik

limit.description: Maximum number of holdings to return. Default 100. Use with offset for pagination. Set higher only when needed — large filers can have 3,000+ positions.
limit.title: Limit

mcp_prompt_id.description: Unique prompt ID for the MCP session. This can be used for tracking and logging purposes. Do not change this value.
mcp_prompt_id.title: Mcp Prompt Id

min_value_thousands.description: Minimum position value in thousands of USD to include. Use to filter out noise: e.g. 1000 = positions worth at least $1M. Default None returns all positions.
min_value_thousands.title: Min Value Thousands

offset.description: Number of holdings to skip before returning results. Use with limit for pagination. Default 0 (start from beginning).
offset.title: Offset

optional_additional_filters.description: Dictionary of additional filters not covered by other fields
optional_additional_filters.title: Optional Additional Filters

question_asked.description: Question asked by the user. Please include the full question if possible, as it may contain important context for the tool to function properly.
question_asked.title: Question Asked

sort_by.description: Sort order for the holdings list. Options: 'value_desc' (largest position first, default), 'value_asc' (smallest first), 'name_asc' (alphabetical by issuer name).
sort_by.title: Sort By

source_resource_id.description:
Optional resource_id of a previously cached result set (returned by a prior Fetch tool call).
        When provided, the tool will load the full dataset directly from the cache folder instead of
        re-executing the query against the database. Pass this when the user is asking a follow-up
        question or a different grouping/filter on data that was already fetched. 
        Also, use this, when one tool output is an input for another tool.
source_resource_id.title: Source Resource Id

wholesaler_ids.description:
List of wholesaler IDs or names to filter results by the internal fin user
        who owns or manages the data. If names are provided instead of IDs, the system will automatically
        resolve them to their corresponding USER_IDs before applying the filter.
        
        In fin, users are assigned one of three roles:
        - Wholesaler: A field-level sales representative responsible for a specific territory, channel,
        or book of accounts. This is the most granular user type. Most sales data, advisor relationships,
        and touchpoints in fin are owned at the wholesaler level.
        - Manager: Oversees a team of Wholesalers, typically organized by territory or sales channel
        (e.g., Regional Manager, Channel Manager). Filtering by a Manager ID will scope results
        to that Manager's purview across their team.
        - Executive: C-suite level users (e.g., CEO, CFO, COO) at the asset manager / fund company
        level (e.g., PIMCO, MetLife, BlackRock). Executives have the broadest visibility and their
        ID represents an org-wide scope.

        Accepts either:
        - User IDs directly (e.g., ['WS001', 'MGR045'])
        - Full or partial user names (e.g., ['John Smith', 'Sarah']) — these will be resolved to IDs
        - A mix of both (e.g., ['WS001', 'Sarah Connor'])

        If omitted, data is returned based on the authenticated user's role and their default data scope.
        Examples: ['WS001'], ['WS001', 'MGR045'], ['John Smith'], ['John Smith', 'WS002']
wholesaler_ids.title: Wholesaler Ids
